newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Caracas stocks end off on correction, higher rates.
newsitem.headline: Caracas stocks end off on correction, higher rates.

text.p: Caracas stocks ended lower for the second consecutive day, after a three-week rally, mainly due to technical adjustments and a rise in six-month TEM yields to 16.48 percent, traders said.
The market's leading 19-share index closed down 100.97 points or 1.48 percent at 6,736.93, according to preliminary figures.
"Basically, the bolsa was down because of the TEMs' higher yields," one trader said.
Central Bank TEM bills are used as a benchmark for wider interest rates.
Ricardo Marino of Intervalores brokerage also explained the drop as a "correction" to the recent long rally.
Other traders noted that despite the Caracas Stock Exchange's spectacular results in 1996, foreign investors had not been very present so far this year.
"Everybody recommends Venezuela, but that's not always put into practice," one said.
